raw_response:
This line plot illustrates the relationship between coverage and the number of completions (k) for four different Llama model configurations: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k),” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 2⁰ (1) to 2⁸ (256), with tick marks at each power of two. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0.2 to 0.9, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The Llama-3B line (solid blue with circular markers) starts at approximately 0.43 at k=1 and increases steadily to about 0.88 at k=256. The Llama-3B + FT line (solid green with triangular markers) begins at roughly 0.42 and rises to approximately 0.89 at k=256, tracking closely above the Llama-3B line across the range. The Llama-1B line (solid light blue with circular markers) starts at about 0.28 and increases to approximately 0.84 at k=256. The Llama-1B + FT line (solid light green with triangular markers) begins at approximately 0.27 and rises to about 0.85 at k=256, remaining slightly above the Llama-1B line throughout. All four lines exhibit a monotonically increasing trend, with steeper growth at lower k values and gradual leveling off as k increases.
